newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa urges private sector housing commitment.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa urges private sector housing commitment.

text.p: Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele on Thursday challenged the private sector to match the government's drive to provide mass low-cost housing.
Addressing a media briefing, Mthembi-Mahanyele said it was appreciated that there were "real risks" involved with low-cost housing but government had done its best to minimise these.
It had provided housing subsidies and political risk guarantees, streamlined procedures, and was itself now starting to deliver mass housing programmes at a quicker pace.
"But it is of some concern to me that there are some in the private sector who seem not to have altered their attitudes," she said.

This was highlighted by the fact that a large European company had been un able to find a local partner to put up 15 percent for a 100 million rand project to build prefabricated houses because the project was aimed at low-cost housing.

Mthembi-Mahanyele said that Standard Bank had decided to consider sympathetically credit applications from customers who could demonstrate that their payment records had been adversely affected by political circumstances prior to April 1994.
"I want to challenge other financial institutions to adopt the same creative, problem-solving attitudes towards low-cost housing."
